flashcards.back: Self-knowledge for the contemplative, and selfless work (Seva, Karma-yoga) for all others.
No one can stay idle even for a moment: the forces of nature drive every being to act.
One who controls the senses with a purified mind and intellect and engages the organs of action in selfless service.
Work not done as selfless service. So work efficiently, free of attachment to fruits, as a service to God.
One who does not help keep it moving by sacrificial duty, living only for sense pleasure, lives in vain.
Janaka and others reached perfection by selfless service alone. Work to guide people and for the welfare of society.
Others follow what the noble do. Even Krishna, with nothing to gain, keeps working to set an example.
The wise should not confuse those attached to results, but inspire them by working well, without attachment.
The energy of nature. Out of ignorance, people think they are the doer and so incur Karmic bondage.
Do your duty in a spiritual frame of mind, free from desire, attachment and grief, offering it all to God.
Even the wise act by their nature. One's own work, even imperfect, is better than forcing a role that isn't one's own.
Likes and dislikes for sense objects. Do not come under their control.
Lust, born of passion, which becomes anger when unfulfilled. It is insatiable: know it as the enemy.
As smoke covers fire, dust a mirror and the amnion an embryo, lust covers Self-knowledge.
Know the Spirit is above the intellect; control the mind with an intellect purified by practice; then slay lust.
Restraining the body while the mind dwells on pleasures is hypocrisy; honest selfless action is better.

quiz.why: Self-knowledge for the contemplative, Karma-yoga for all others.

quiz.text: What does 3.9 say binds human beings?

options.B: Work not done as selfless service

quiz.why: Selfish work binds; work done as service to God frees.

quiz.text: Why does Krishna keep working though he has nothing to gain?
quiz.why: Whatever the great do, others follow.
Nature acts; the deluded ego claims to be the doer.

quiz.text: What should the wise do with people attached to results?

options.C: Inspire them by working without attachment

quiz.why: 3.26: don't unsettle their minds; set the example.

quiz.text: What are the two great stumbling blocks of 3.34?
quiz.why: Attraction and aversion for sense objects.

quiz.text: What veils Self-knowledge like smoke over fire?
What is higher than the intellect, per 3.43?
quiz.why: Knowing the Spirit is above the intellect, control the mind and kill lust.

options.A: One who doesn't help turn the wheel of creation

quiz.why: Living only for pleasure, without sacrificial duty, breaks the cycle.
